This meeting was concluded without specific conclusions and members of the joint command went back. But from the point in time when Travnik was occupied, Croatian members, that is members of the HVO, had no access to the joint command headquarters. In other words, they were unable to go there to attend meetings and go on about their work.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could I please have the Exhibit number D370 shown to the witness? While we're waiting for it, perhaps we can take a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we could have our regular break of 15 minutes. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. I think Judge Rodrigues would like to ask three questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Sorry for the microphone. Thank you. General Blaskic, before going on, I would like to ask you three questions. You mentioned the date of the 28th of May. You said that two houses of two HVO officers were occupied by Croats; you remember? There was one apartment and a house which were used by two HVO officers and these two places were occupied?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: My question is this: Do you know if the individuals who occupied these houses, or the apartment and the house, knew that these were places where HVO officers lived?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know whether they knew or not, but I was informed that they were refugees who, quite simply, had come there, occupied the apartment, that is to say, the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. My second question is the following: On the 12th of June, you mentioned that there was a convoy of refugees; am I right? You gave some explanations. Mr. Thebault told you that it was not convenient to do this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps if it was a matter of a convoy, the humanitarian aid Tuzla convoy, I think I spoke of the 11th of June perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes, the 11th of June. You're right. Yes, it took place on the 11th of June, but I think it was a convoy of refugees, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Perhaps it was interpreted incorrectly. The refugees had blocked the roads, and at the request of Mr. Thebault, I went to bring back the convoy, so we came across this section of the road that was blocked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: All right. I'm sorry, I didn't understand well what you said. However, I will take this opportunity to ask you this question: These refugees, were they Croats, Muslims? What was their nationality?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They belonged mostly -- that is to say, they were mostly Croats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps some mixed marriages, Your Honour, but mostly Croats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes. My third question is the following: We've seen this map, document number D458, and referring to this map, you said that the enemy was always the army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That, for the most part, it was the army of the Republika Srpska, but at one point it was attacked and I was brought into this situation by the BH army, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: It means that at that stage you changed your position, or you still thought that your main enemy was the army of the Republika Srpska, or then you started thinking that the enemy was the BH army.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For me as a soldier brought into the position of fighting for my life, biologically speaking in this situation, for me the adversary was the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in that particular situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To follow on from that question, what was your aim during peacetime? Did you have any idea that things would end up as they ended up while there was still peace?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean between the BH army and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I think that the joint command of the 3rd Corps and the HVO for the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, which worked until the beginning of the attack on Travnik, that is to say, the 3rd of June, 1993, has documents on a jointly planned operation against the army of the Republika Srpska at Mount Vlasic, and we took part in an elaboration of the plan to free Vlasic. The 3rd Corps and the command of the Operative Zone worked together on this plan. Franjo Nakic and Dzemo Merdan worked together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move on to document D370. I'm not going to read all of it out, just parts of the document. It's dated the 16th of June, 1993, and you wrote it. It is your order to all the brigades and independent units. I'm going to read the last point: "Based on the General Agreement on cessation of conflict in Bosnina and Herzegovina of 15 June 1993, signed by Major-General Milivoj Petkovic, Brigadier-General Ratko Mladic, and General Rasim Delic, witnessed by UNPROFOR members Brigadier-General Lars-Eric Wahlgren, deputy Chief of Mission Cedric Thornberry and Brigadier-General Phillippe Morillon, Commander of UNPROFOR for Bosnia-Herzegovina. "I hereby order." And now a series of points within that order linked to the cease-fire, and I am going to read points 6, 7 and 8. "6. To allow the passage of humanitarian aid and freedom of movement to the representatives of international humanitarian organisations along with the usual control measures. 7. Electricity, water, and telephones should not be used as weapons and efforts should be taken to maintain all facilities supplying water and electricity. 8. Lists with all prisoners of war and any of those killed under their authority should be sent to the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and the names of the officers are stipulated and the telephone numbers. 9. All HVO units of Central Bosnia Operative Zone are duty-bound by the Geneva Conventions of the 12th --" We cannot read the month, but the year is 1949. "-- and the additional protocols, as well as other instruments pertaining to wartime law and the protection of human rights. 10. For the implementation of this order, the commanders of brigades and independent units of the 3rd Operative Zone shall be responsible to me." The commander is Colonel Blaskic. Tell us, please, General, under what circumstances was this order issued and compiled?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The order came into being under the conditions of a signed truce on a cessation of hostilities on the basis of an agreement reached by three commanders, that is, the commanders of three armies, as can be seen, the chief of the main staff of the HVO, then the commander of the Republika Srpska, and the commander of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to show you another document, D371. The document is D371, and it seems it was written on the 19th of June, 1993, although the date is not very legible, at 15.55, and the text reads as follows: "Pursuant to the agreement signed on cessation of hostilities in Bosnia and Herzegovina --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can you hear anything? Good, Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Pursuant to the signed agreements on a cessation of hostilities in Bosnia and Herzegovina dated the 10th and 15th of June and the agreement with the opposite side, on the operationalisation of the agreement from Vitez dated the 10th of June, 1993, I hereby order: 1. To prevent the arrest of civilians as a function of wartime operations in the form of taking them prisoner and taking hostages and to weaken -- allegedly to weaken the enemy ..." Something has been added here in writing by hand, I cannot read it, it is illegible, but perhaps you can read it because the copy is not a very good one.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is my own handwriting, and it says "... in towns and villages which are under the exclusive control of the HVO of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I now go on to point 2 which has been typed and is legible. "2. To prevent the burning of facilities and the destruction of material goods, especially to protect religious facilities such as mosques, the mejtefs, the vakuf, and the mezars. 3. Any appropriation of property should be sanctioned and should be solved by military disciplinary measures and through the prosecution and the courts. 4. For the implementation of these orders, the commanders of brigades shall be responsible to me and the commanders of independent units, and I should be informed as to the implementation of my orders." It is signed Colonel Tihomir Blaskic. Tell us, please, General, we have new conflicts in June. Why did you order that civilians cannot be taken prisoner? Isn't that something that is common knowledge and prohibited by law?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is common knowledge, but I have already said that in this enclave, a large number of refugees carrying weapons had arrived and with military equipment and carrying little bags in their hands, and there were incidents of various kinds because, as I say, there were perhaps 20.000 or more displaced persons, and I tried to enforce preventive measures in order to rein in any of these incidents or reactions that could have been expected from them towards the Bosniak Muslims who still lived in the area of the Lasva River Valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, you asked that burning of facilities be prevented as well as the destruction of material property, this you said in point 2 of your order, but you mention separately the religious buildings. Could you explain in brackets whose places of worship these were and to whom they belonged?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They belonged to the Islamic religious community, and I separated them and highlighted them because from the 3rd of June, there were various rumours and information circulated that the BH army had killed priests in the parishes of Brajkovici and Grahovcici and that a church had been burned down and so on and so forth, and it was already common knowledge that the 3rd Corps had put some of its forces into Guca Gora in the convent there, that they had taken it over, and I tried to enforce preventive measures to stop the reactions of Croats in areas controlled by the HVO and retaliation and revenge for activities of that type.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You enumerate four types of places of worship of the Islamic religion. Can you tell us what they represent? We know "dzamija" is "mosque." Can you explain the other three terms you use?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the mezars were the cemeteries, they were cemeteries or graves, tombstones of Bosniak Muslims. The mejtef, as far as I know, were the buildings for worship, places of worship heretofore, as well as vakufs. A vakuf is an area owned by the Islamic religious community. Mosques, of course, are a place, a house of worship where religious customs are enacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Nobilo. I have some questions about dates. I didn't note that the cease-fire had been signed on the 15th of June; however, the two documents that you've just presented refer to a cease-fire signed on the 15th of June. You mention that there was a cease-fire ordered by Alija Izetbegovic on the 13th of June, and I noted on the 14th of June at 14.00 hours, there was a cease-fire as well. So are you referring to the one of the 14th of June, because on the 15th of June, you had a meeting with Mr. Thebault, Enver Hadzihasanovic did not attend this meeting, you're asking for some food aid to the UNHCR, there was a meeting with the Red Cross as well. So my question is: Was this cease-fire signed on the 15th of June? Maybe there's a mistake in my notes.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is not an error, Mr. President, yours is not an error. The general agreement on a cease-fire was signed on the 15th of June, 1993, by the three military commanders, and I know, according to my notes, that there was also a meeting on the 10th of June of the military commanders, but I do not know if they signed an agreement on that occasion, or perhaps on the 10th of June they just had a meeting, and then the 15th of June, agreement was a result of that previous meeting. But the general cease-fire agreement was signed on the 15th of June, 1993, and it is Defence Exhibit 370.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we can explain in the following way: Is there a notion of a general cease-fire agreement between all three conflicting sides, the Serbs, the Croats, and the Muslims, and whether there were cease-fires between the Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, there was a general cease-fire agreement of the 15th of June between three hostile parties, warring parties, and there was an agreement between the Croats and the Muslims as well which was signed I think in Vitez, but I can't see the date very well here, whether it was the 10th or the 19th of June. I think it was the 19th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go on with the chronology of events. Then we may come back to this later.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 17th of June, 1993, in the morning at about 6.55, the BH army continued its offensive operations in the municipality of Novi Travnik and, at about 8.00, the other areas of Travnik municipality. In the course of the day of the 17th of June, in the afternoon, I was visited by Colonel Duncan, and I had a conversation with him when I thanked him for providing security for Croats in Guca Gora and for other things, and we also discussed the question of civilian and military HVO casualties. According to my records, from the 10th of June until the 17th of June, '93, UNPROFOR forces had killed 17 Croats, both civilians and military men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you use this word in B/C/S, it means both wounded and dead.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Some of them were wounded and died from the consequences and some of them were killed, including some Croats at the time of the attack on the convoy, that is, the night between the 10th and the 11th of June -- yes, June 1993. In the course of this conversation, Colonel Duncan asked me, and I quote, "Your HVO forces from Prozor, are they going to make a breakthrough to the Lasva Valley and lift the siege that you're in?" My answer to Colonel Duncan was that he knew very well that a truce had been signed between the BH army and the HVO, and I also added that I didn't have any information about any planned breakthrough from Prozor into the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of your overall knowledge, was ever an attempt made to deblock and free the Lasva Valley or, rather, the enclave in Central Bosnia by HVO troops from the south of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I also added at that meeting with Colonel Duncan that I was aware that we were totally surrounded and that our situation was virtually hopeless, and Colonel Duncan said to me, "I do not believe that you will be able to bear out," and that is how we ended this meeting on the 17th of June, 1993. On the 18th of June, the BH army continued its attacks against the Frankopan Brigade or, rather, against the remaining territory we held, that is, about 10 per cent of Travnik municipality, and throughout the day there was fighting over the Pescara feature. On the 20th of June, 1993, the BH army, via Igman, repositioned the 101st and 102nd Brigades from Sarajevo, or parts of those brigades, and formed an operative group of the 6th Corps and parts of the 1st Corps, and I received information that they would be engaged in the continuation of the offensive. At my morning briefing with my associates, the chief of staff, Mr. Franjo Nakic, complained and said that ever since the 11th of February, 1993, he was working together with Dzemo Merdan in joint commissions and the joint command and that his associates in the staff were complaining because of his protracted absence. The period from the 20th to the 23rd of June I spent at the Pescara feature, and these were days of intensified defence. These are the positions marked with the blue flag (indicating). This is the remaining part of Travnik municipality that we still controlled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you show it, please?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us look at two other documents from that period. The first is D372.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, Exhibit D372, the date is illegible, but one may assume it was sometime around the 19th of June in view of the registration number, and you say: "Pursuant to agreements reached by the joint command of the BH army, the commander of the 3rd Operational Zone of Central Bosnia, and the commander of the 3rd Corps of the BH army, I hereby issue the following order: 1. Ensure unhindered passage of the convoy of food to the village of Kruscica on the 21st of June, 1993, which will be escorted by the UNHCR, the International Red Cross, and the European Monitoring Mission." And then you go on to say that mines have to be cleared and that the police have to make sure that this is carried out. Tell us, which forces were in Kruscica? Whose forces were there and which ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Most of the 325th Mountain Brigade of the BH army from Vitez were there, as well as reinforcements from the 308th Mountain Brigade from Novi Travnik, and the majority population or, rather, the only population living there at the time were Bosniak Muslims. As for mines and other things, these were mostly along the front lines, and the convoy was to have passed across front lines held by the HVO and a second front line held by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please, number D373.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is an order which is again not too legible. I shall try to read the parts that are legible. The document is D373. It has a date, the 21st June, 1993, and it is addressed to all brigade commanders and wardens of military prisons. The heading is "Treatment of Prisoners of War." And it says: "Based on the provisions of the Geneva Conventions of 12th August, 1949, which regulate the treatment of prisoners of war, I hereby order: 1. The treatment of prisoners of war...," and then a couple of words are illegible and then it says that, "...mistreatment, beating, and psychological torture are forbidden." Then in point 2 it says: "2. I forbid the use of prisoners of war for engineering projects on the territory, digging shelters, trench cover-ups, road bunkers, et cetera. 3. I draw attention of brigade commanders" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, just a moment, please. There's a problem of translation into French. I prefer the translation I was given on the basis your reading. It talks about engineering projects here, but one can understand, though it is a big word, I prefer the French. It is really not a question of large scale engineering works, it is more engineers' projects, in military terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, that is what it says here, engineers' projects. It is a military term referring to the digging of trenches, shelters, bunkers, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we come to point 3: "3. The attention of brigade commanders and military prison wardens is drawn to the fact that the use of prisoners of war as a work-force for engineering projects on the territory constitutes a war crime and that an international court for war crimes has been formed which will investigate and sanction such treatment. 4. I hold responsible brigade commanders and wardens of military prisons for the implementation of this order. Commander, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic." General, were you referring to this Tribunal when you threatened your commanders with an international court?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you then already received some information? Why did you use this term? Why did you refer to the fact that an international court had been formed, in an order of this kind?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had tried to act preventatively and to exert pressure on commanders, fully aware of the overall situation we found ourselves in, and I used all means at my disposal to prevent violations of the provisions of the Geneva Conventions and other humanitarian laws and international war law in circumstances I was in at the time in June 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why then did you use this fact that the court had been founded?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I just wanted to address myself to General Blaskic. Did Colonel Duncan speak to you about the formation of the Tribunal or Mr. Thebault or did you learn from the media, from the press, about it? Were you told by members of the UNPROFOR, by Colonel Duncan, for instance, about the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mr. President, I never discussed this Tribunal with Colonel Duncan. I know that the assistant for information had conveyed to me the information that this Tribunal had been formed. He must have heard it from the media. I have no record in my notes that I spoke to Mr. Thebault about this Tribunal either. From the press I couldn't learn about it because there was no press at that time in our region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your officer for information and propaganda activities informed you about this, but why did you put that fact in this order? What was the aim you were trying to achieve by threatening your commanders with this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I wanted to prevent any acts which were war crimes, because I said that my most important task was to prevent a repetition of crimes, under those circumstances, in the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're addressing this to brigade commanders but also to the prison warden. Were you the superior of the prison warden or did you write this to him on some other grounds?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a preventative order. I just asked -- I was just looking for a way of informing the prison warden of my position and of my warnings. I was not his superior. I was aware of that fact, that I wasn't the superior of the prison warden, but I wanted to inform the prison warden too of my personal position and my position in relation to the International War Crimes Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please, D374.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is another in a series of orders issued on the 19th of June, 1993. It is addressed to several addressees. I'm not going to read that out. Let me just read two points from this order, which is the substance of the order. First: "I prohibit evictions of non-Croat inhabitants from family homes and apartments in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. 2. Provide maximum security for non-Croats in towns and villages under the exclusive control of the units and authorities of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia and of the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna," and you make commanders responsible to you, mentioning the army, the HVO, the military, the civilian police, et cetera. What prompted you to issue this order? It was not the first, but why did you issue this order on the 19th of June, '93?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have said that we had the problem of a large number of exiles and that the civilian authorities, even if it had functioned in the best possible manner, it simply did not have the facilities to accommodate so many refugees. So again, I tried to act in a preventive manner and to prevent any action, I could even call it attempts at revenge by Croatian refugees towards non-Croats living in the areas under the control of the HVO. These were, in most cases, Bosniak Muslims, but there were also Serbs and there were also Gypsies or Romanies. We had also reached agreement within the joint command to prevent any such activity, that is, mutual expulsions, evictions and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please, D375, dated the 21st of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an order issued by the commander of the 2nd Battalion of the Vitez Brigade, and on the basis of the order of the commander of the Vitez Brigade, he orders the following, I'm just going to read out a couple of points: "1. Prevent arrest of civilians and the taking of hostages intended to weaken the enemy in the areas controlled by units of the 2nd Battalion. 2. Prevent the torching of buildings and the destruction of property, and in particular, protect places of worship, mosques, mejtefs, vakufs, and mezars. 3. All appropriations and robberies must be severely punished and dealt with by military disciplinary measures, by the public Prosecutors' offices, and the courts. 4. Do not permit any mistreatment of prisoners and immediately make records of any such mistreatment," and so on and so forth. Do you recognise in this order a literal copy of entire sentences from another order? What does this tell you regarding the chain of command and the transfer of orders?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Obviously, that the battalion commander here has literally copied the order of the brigade commander. If we were to take the order that was on the ELMO a moment ago, then we see that this is a copy of the same, that is, the battalion commander has copied the brigade commander's order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your view, whose order was copied?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In this case, my order. But our greatest problem was with the implementation of orders. That is where the difficulties arose. If we were to see on the ground what the impact of this order was, we would see the problems because I am familiar with the area of responsibility of this battalion. It is, in fact, the northern part of Vitez, which was most frequently the target of attack by BH army units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, did you require that the order that you issued at the level of the Operative Zone should be implemented right down the chain of command and should be conveyed to the soldier at the bottom of the line?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That can be seen from the documents. When I asked that the order should be conveyed on to the lower levels, with a signature, which would mean that the battalion commander would have to sign to confirm that he had received it and that he must have the certification that the battalion commander had received the order. I required the same procedure to be applied right down the line, that the battalion commander should insist that the low-level commanders had received such an order and that they should confirm it with their signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Shall we have a break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. We're going to have a 15-minute break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let us resume the hearing. Please be seated. Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let's continue with the chronology of events? A. On the 23rd of June, 1993, I received information from the chief of the Military Intelligence Service that the president of the district military court was wounded, this was Mr. Percinlic. There were gunshot wounds to both of his feet. It was committed by criminals by shooting at him from close range, from several metres. On the 24th of June, 1993, an all-out attack by the BH army, that is, its 3rd Corps, was launched against the HVO in Zepce, and this date was probably picked up for a reason, with good reason, because that was the day of pilgrimage to Zepce when most Croats go to the Brankovac parish for the holiday of St. Ivo. At 12.30, I had a meeting with Mr. de la Mota, and he asked that I provide assistance for the passage of a convoy which was destined for Zenica through Vitez. I do not recall where the convoy was coming from; I have not noted it down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you provide assistance for the safe passage of this convoy?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I provided assistance, but I don't know specifically where the convoy was coming from. On the 26th of June, 1993, I had a meeting with Mr. de la Mota --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This was in the zones under your control, I assume? Yes?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. To assist him with the passage of a convoy through an area controlled by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Go on.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 25th of June, 1993, I had a meeting with Mr. de la Mota, and he informed me that he had difficulties in carrying out his duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That he had problems with Croats?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, with Croats. That his movements were being monitored and that people were shouting at him, that he was noticing a change of behaviour compared to what the behaviour was before. I told him that the Lasva Valley was full of refugees, that these are desperate people, and that it would be good if he addressed the population through the local media and to explain what his mandate was and the nature of his mission because these were mostly people who had been driven out from Novi Travnik, Travnik, and Zenica, these were Croats who probably did not know very well what the mandate of the International Committee of the Red Cross and the UNHCR and other international institutions was. I also told Mr. de la Mota that I had personally organised a seminar for my staff in order to inform them about the mandate of the international institutions but that it would be much better and more efficient if he himself could address the population of the Lasva Valley through the local television. This is what he did in the following days. He was a guest of Vitez Television, and I think that his appearance there and the explanations he gave at that time had an effect. I also pointed out a problem which by that time had spread, and that was that whenever food arrived through the international organisations in Kruscica, after the convoy passed and carried out its mission, the BH army from Kruscica almost, as a rule, opened fire on the settlements around Vitez or Vitez itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was this interpreted in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: What the people thought, how they understood it was that these organisations had delivered ordinance, ammunition, and they insisted that their representatives monitor these deliveries so as to be sure that along with humanitarian aid, no ammunition was also being delivered. I even told Mr. de la Mota that there is a good road from Novi Travnik to Kruscica via Opara and that we could use that road for deliveries to Kruscica if we were unable to resolve the problem with the behaviour of civilians. I also asked Mr. de la Mota to help provide assistance with delivery of clothes, evacuation of wounded, and that he should visit Vares, Travnik, Novi Travnik, and Zenica. On the 25th of June, 1993, early in the morning, Sebesic was attacked, this is an area due south-east of Novi Travnik, and the HVO lost its positions there and pulled back in the direction of Gornji Vakuf along with Croats from Sebesic, Ravno Rostovo, and other areas. This evacuation of civilians was assisted by the UNPROFOR from Vakuf who provided protection for civilians as they were withdrawing. In the course of 25 June, we were forced to deploy some of the civilian police forces at the line of defence so that only the chief of the police station and an associate of his, a lady, remained in the police station, and everybody else went to the front line. In the area controlled by the HVO, a vehicle was taken from a judge of the district military court, and he himself was physically attacked and beaten up by a gang of criminals. On that day, I also received information that Ivan Ravlic, the priest, was again detained and brought to questioning by the SIS centre, and the priest came to me himself and cried as he related the story of his mistreatment. On the 26th of June, 1993, I received information from the security service that a private businessman in Vitez had manufactured a multiple rocket launcher, and they kept it in their possession. I ordered that this weapon be taken from them and that it be given to the Vitez Brigade for use. This was later carried out. On the 27th of June, 1993, I asked for information about single-barrel rocket launchers which were also being produced in dozens, first in the weapons factory in Travnik and then in Vitez. I was informed by the commander of the Vitez Brigade, also on the 27th of June, that this multiple rocket launcher had been taken from this private group. Also on the 27th of June, I attempted, through the main staff, to learn what was going on in Zepce and what the military situation in Zepce was. On the 30th of June, 1993, I was informed by the chief of the Military Intelligence Service that he had information that the soldier Ivan Dzilic Bukal had been taken as a prisoner of war in the Travnik barracks and that he had been killed overnight and his body taken to the front line and dumped there. On the 1st of July, 1993, I requested information about the investigation of the robbery of the Tuzla convoy from the security service. On the 3rd of July, there was shelling of Vitez by the BH army with shells which had additional chlorine filling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in any way record this fact, that chlorine was used as a charge in these shells?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We just had suspicions and we passed them on to the UNPROFOR, and we also compiled medical information on the basis of examination of the injured and attached it to all the other information we had gathered and sent it off to UNPROFOR. On the 4th of July, 1993, I received information from the Military Intelligence Service that the BH army was grouping significant forces in the village of Zivcici, which was in the Fojnica municipality, and that it was bearing forces for offensive operations probably in the direction of Fojnica, and from the security service I was informed that three members of the Vitezovi had committed suicide while on duty with that unit. On the 5th of July, 1993, I was informed that the BH army had attacked the HVO units in the village of Dezevice, this is in the municipality of Kresevo, and that it had driven out both the HVO units and the civilians also fled and arrived in the town of Kresevo. On the 6th of July, 1993, I asked for the involvement of the military police and the civilian police regarding the killing of the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit about the killing of this interpreter and what happened?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Her name was Dobrila, and I think it was near the officers' club of the UN forces. I think it was near this UN officers' club in Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know any circumstances of this killing?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: She was killed by snipers from an area which we assessed should have been demilitarised from the 24th of -- from April 1993, after the cease-fire was agreed to. On the 8th of July, 1993, the BH army carried out an attack on the north-western approaches of the town of Vitez from the direction of Zenica. Also, about ten truckloads of soldiers arrived to the positions at Grbavica; and on the 9th of July, I received a report on the robbery of a Tuzla convoy, and I asked for more detailed information because it was just sketchy information, and this information reached me through the security service. On the 10th of July, 1993, the BH army again attacked from the direction of Zenica on the town of Vitez. On the 11th of July, 1993, the BH army carried out an artillery attack on the part of the town of Novi Travnik controlled by the HVO. A civilian was killed. On that day, I sent a written memorandum to the chief of the main quarters of the HVO insisting that he release the military police commander, that he fire the staff, and that he carries out a reorganisation of the military police, including giving me the command of the military police. On the 12th of July, 1993, our telephone links with the UN were cut off, and according to the information which I received, they were cut off in Stari Vitez. In the course of the day, I had a meeting with the official of the UN Monitoring Mission. This was Mr. Stavros. He transmitted to me the position of Commander Alagic, in which Alagic asked of me to move his positions in Puticevo forward at the expense of the HVO by some 300 metres. I told Mr. Stavros that if I was allowed, that I might as well give up the defence of Novi Travnik because this would amount to a surrender of Novi Travnik and Novi Travnik municipality. So I could not agree to such a request, and I let the representative of the European Monitoring Mission know of that. I also had a meeting with a representative of the monitoring mission from Zagreb. I believe his name was Deer or something like that, I'm not sure. He asked me to give him an update on the situation in the Lasva Valley. At 19.00, I received information from Nakic on the activities of the joint command, which had resumed its work based on the agreement of June 1993. On the 14th of July, 1993, I asked an investigation from the security service regarding the killing of the Mujkic family from Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnic group were the Mujkics?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were Bosnian Muslims. And on the 15th of July, 1993, at 9.00 in the morning, the BH army opened artillery fire as well as tank fire at the centre of Vitez. During the day, I also asked for investigation of the murder of Ciklas, and learned that Radinko Skoro, Mirko Kvasina, and a man last named Jotland (phoen), I don't have the first name, were suspects.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the victim was a Bosniak Muslim?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the victim was a Bosniak Muslim and the perpetrators were Croats?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We need to slow down because the interpreters and court reporters are not able to keep pace.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On 16th July, 1993, I was told that the HVO had lost its positions in Fojnica and that the HVO units had pulled back from Fojnica, along with the civilians, and that they had pulled back into the area of Kresevo and Kiseljak to the areas controlled by the HVO. In the course of the day of 16 July there was another attack against Dominik Sakic, HVO president in Zenica, and Zivko Totic. They were attacked and physically abused. Persons called Zaga, Jole, and Ramljak. On the 17th of July, 1993, the BH army launched an artillery attack against Vitez but I have no information on casualties, but I have recorded that there had been casualties. Also, BH army had offensive operations in Novi Travnik and Zepce. I asked for information from the security service about what measures were taken against the attackers on Sakic, and Totic, and the Tuzla convoy attack. On 21 July, 1993, I again requested an update on the investigation of the security service regarding the Mujkic family murders. On that day, early in the morning, we had an attack against the villages of Zabilje and the northern defence line of Vitez and parts of the Novi Travnik municipality. On the 22nd of July, 1993, sometime after 12.00, strong explosions could be heard in the explosives factory. A large amount of explosives had exploded spontaneously in an area called Susine. Fortunately, there were no casualties. I contacted Lido Dragan Kvasina, who was a legal advisor, and I was looking for legal assistance even though it was not proper for me to do so, but I wanted him let me know about the legal proceedings, disciplinary measures, and maintenance of law and order. What I wanted was for him to organise seminars so that we would educate our staff about disciplinary measures and of processing of disciplinary measures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The name of the legal advisor whom you hired on your own?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: His name was Dragan Kvasina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody else in any other Operative Zone have such a staff position?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he start working for you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On that day he started work. He was a disabled person and he wanted to work, and I had need for such a person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he, from that moment on, become a member of the headquarters of the staff?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On that day, there were attacks on Novi Vitez and Travnik by the BH army, and this period is -- can be characterised by these offensive operations, but it was predominantly artillery attacks and less infantry attacks. I also received information and transmitted it through the liaison officer to the UNHCR of the UN that the hospital in Pakovici was without water supplies and that the safety of about 520 patients was threatened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, let me stop you here for a moment and take you back to a document that was issued on 20th June, 1993. We have it in all three versions, in all three languages, and I would like it distributed appropriately. This is the best copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we have the number of the exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 549, 549A for the French version, and 549B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me read the document. It is a short one. The Croatian Defence Council, Vitez, 20th of June, 1993, and the heading is "Certificate." "Whereby the special purpose unit Vitezovi, PPN Vitezovi" -- "Certificate: Whereby the Vitezovi, the unit for special purposes, confirms that the apartment at Marshall Tito Street, number B-4/22, occupied by Mahmut and Javra Tuco shall not be appropriated and that the same people will continue to use it. This certificate is issued for the purpose of protection against eviction. Colonel Darko Kraljevic," and a stamp which says, "Defence Department, Special Purpose Unit Vitezovi, Vitez." Above that it says, "Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna." General, do you recognise this signature it says here of Colonel Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise his signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this his signature?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the stamp that he used?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is his stamp, the stamp of the Special Purpose Unit Vitezovi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mahmut and Javra Tuco? What ethnic group do they belong to?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They are Muslims, Bosniaks. The Tuco family is a family whose name I know from Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to the court how did it happen that a special purpose unit, the Vitezovi or, rather, Colonel Darko Kraljevic, decide who would be evicted or who would not be evicted from his own apartment? Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was behaviour contrary to my orders, and even this certificate is an indication of his autonomy, and independence, and the fact that he engaged in activities beyond his sphere of competence, because the Tuco family are probably not his soldiers, and a military commander has no competence regarding the confiscation or return of apartments of civilians. At least I was never aware of any such authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does such a certificate tell you about the position of Darko Kraljevic and how he was treated by the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is certainly a reflection of his power and his complete independence of any other institution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you think: If Darko Kraljevic were to protect somebody for some reason, would this be respected? For instance, could these people be evicted after such a certificate?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. This is the most powerful document for a family who had possession of it. It gave that family complete protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue with the chronology or perhaps we could close there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Have you finished with the 22nd of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: With the document or do you have more questions about the 22nd of July? Perhaps let us finish off with that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No, no more questions about the 22nd of July or this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. In that case, we are going to adjourn for various and multiple reasons. First of all, the health of General Blaskic. Were you able to see the nurse this morning? Were you treated this morning? Did everything go well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, for your inquiry. Yes, I was treated for my eye. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Tomorrow morning the Chamber will still be dealing with the Blaskic case but without Mr. Blaskic, so you will have a long weekend. On the other hand, some Judges are engaged in another case on the 22nd and the 23rd of this month, so we'll continue with the Prosecution tomorrow morning at 9.30. Is that right, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Secondly, as regards the continuation and the position of the accused as a witness, we will resume on Wednesday (sic) the 23rd at 2.30. Mr. Hayman? Yes, Mr. Hayman? So we will not be sitting on Monday afternoon and Tuesday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I'm just slightly confused, Mr. President. The 23rd is Tuesday. The transcript says, "Wednesday the 23rd," and the schedule we've been given is we will be sitting in the afternoon on Tuesday, the 23rd. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, quite correct. That is what I just said, 2.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The English translation is we would continue on Wednesday --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No. I think that the reporters are this tired, as General Blaskic, as the Judges, as you, for that matter. We will be resuming on Tuesday the 23rd at 2.30 rather than 2.00, because one of our colleagues will be sitting all morning in another case. Therefore, the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: at 5.32 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of March, 1999 at 2.30 p.m. 22 23 24 25
